context: In fact, our algorithm solves also the general canonization problem, see Section 5.4. We remark that the algorithm of Theorem 3 is non-uniform, in the sense that we obtain a different algorithm for every class C . Despite the existence of parameters such as rankdepth [22] or SC-depth [17] that are suited for the treatment of single graphs and are equivalent in terms of boundedness on classes to shrubdepth, we do not know how to make our algorithm uniform even for the rankdepth or SC-depth parameterizations. Finally, we believe that the construction behind our proof of Theorem 2 can be used to obtain an alternative proof of a result of Hliněný and Gajarský [13], later reproved by Chen and Flum [8]: the expressive power of first-order and monadic second-order logic coincide on classes of bounded shrubdepth.
